label: Casimir Oyelaran, procurement lead - saved 25 Sep
text:
Six checks I run before I approve any vendor contract.

1. Who signs on their side, and can that person actually commit the company?
2. What happens to our data on the day we leave?
3. Is the renewal price written down, or only the first-year price?
4. Which of their other customers our size can I phone?
5. What did the last outage look like, and who told whom?
6. If the account manager leaves, who knows our setup?

The fourth one has ended more deals than the other five together.

Which check would you add?

label: Sunniva Achterberg, people director - saved 27 Sep
text:
A founder asked me last week whether she should hire a head of sales before she'd closed ten deals herself.

I said no, and then spent the weekend wondering if that was just what I'd been told at her stage.

So here is the longer answer. Until you have sold it yourself you can't tell a good salesperson from a confident one, and you can't tell a bad quarter from a bad product.

Ten is arbitrary. The point is that it has to be enough for you to have lost a few.

label: own post, 30 Sep
text:
My bet: by the end of next year, most first-round interviews at companies our size will be asynchronous.

We moved ours in April. Candidates record answers to three written questions in their own time. Scheduling used to take a median of six days; now there isn't any.

What would change my mind: if offer acceptance drops. So far it hasn't moved.

P.S. Two candidates told us they preferred a call. We gave them one.
